questions.question:
A stopwatch is used to record the exact time (in seconds)
it takes students to run 100 metres.
Is this numerical data 'discrete' or 'continuous'?
questions.worked_solution: Time is measured on a continuous scale rather than counted in whole numbers, so it is continuous numerical data.

questions.question:
Find the mode of the following dataset:
7, 4, 9, 4, 6, 4, 8, 9
questions.worked_solution: The mode is the most frequent score. The number 4 appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.question:
A survey asks customers to rate service as:
'Poor', 'Fair', 'Good', or 'Excellent'.
What specific type of categorical data is this
('nominal' or 'ordinal')?
questions.worked_solution: Because the categories have a natural, logical order from lowest to highest rating, the data is ordinal.

questions.question:
Find the range of the following daily maximum
temperatures (in °C):
14, 29, 18, 35, 22, 11

Find the median of the following 6 test scores:
19, 12, 25, 14, 28, 17
questions.worked_solution: Ordered scores: 12, 14, 17, 19, 25, 28. The middle two scores are 17 and 19. Median = (17 + 19) ÷ 2 = 18.

questions.question:
Find the median of the following 7 scores:
23, 15, 31, 19, 27, 12, 25
questions.worked_solution: Ordered scores: 12, 15, 19, 23, 25, 27, 31. The middle (4th) score is 23.

questions.question:
Using this stem-and-leaf plot of 15 exam results,
calculate the Range of the data.
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a stem-and-leaf plot. Stem 7 | Leaf 0  7  8. Stem 8 | Leaf 0  0  5  5  5  8  8  9. Stem 9 | Leaf 2  4  5  5. Include 'Key: 7 | 0 = 70'.]

questions.question:
Calculate the mean of these 5 test scores:
64, 72, 80, 68, 76

A frequency table shows quiz scores out of 5:
Score 1 (freq 2), Score 2 (freq 4), Score 5 (freq 4).
Calculate the mean score.

A dot plot records the number of pets for 10 families:
0 pets (2 dots), 1 pet (4 dots),
2 pets (3 dots), and 5 pets (1 dot).
Calculate the mean number of pets per family.

In a frequency histogram, most of the data is clustered
on the left with a long tail stretching out to the right.
Is this distribution 'positively skewed',
'negatively skewed', or 'symmetrical'?
questions.worked_solution: A distribution follows the direction of its tail. A long tail to the right (towards higher positive values) is positively skewed.

questions.question:
Class A (12 students) has a mean test score of 75.
Class B (8 students) has a mean test score of 85.
What is the combined mean for all 20 students?

A dataset containing 5 numbers has a mean of 17.
Four of the numbers are 12, 15, 18, and 21.
What is the 5th number?
questions.worked_solution: Total of all 5 numbers = 5 × 17 = 85. Sum of known 4 numbers = 12 + 15 + 18 + 21 = 66. Missing number = 85 − 66 = 19.

questions.question:
6 tradies have a mean daily wage of $200.
A 7th tradie joins the crew, and the new mean daily wage
for all 7 tradies becomes $210.
How much does the 7th tradie earn?

8 students score a mean of 72 on a mathematics test.
When an outlier score of 30 is removed from the dataset,
what is the new mean of the remaining 7 students?
questions.worked_solution: Original sum = 8 × 72 = 576. New sum after removing 30 = 576 − 30 = 546. New mean = 546 ÷ 7 = 78.

questions.question:
Five positive integers in ascending order are: 6, 8, x, 14, y.
The median of the dataset is 11 and the mean is 12.
Find the value of y.
questions.worked_solution: Since the 5 scores are in order, the 3rd score is the median, so x = 11. Total sum = 5 × 12 = 60. Therefore, 6 + 8 + 11 + 14 + y = 60 → 39 + y = 60 → y = 21.

questions.question:
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
A pair of equal angles form a 'Z' shape on opposite sides
of the transversal between the parallel lines.
Are they 'alternate', 'corresponding', or 'co-interior'?
questions.worked_solution: Angles on opposite sides of the transversal inside the parallel lines (forming a Z shape) are alternate angles.

questions.question:
Two angles are complementary (they add to 90°).
If one angle measures 34°,
what is the size of the other angle?

Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
One of the co-interior angles measures 68°.
What is the size of the other co-interior angle?
questions.worked_solution: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary (add to 180°). 180° − 68° = 112°.

questions.question:
Three angles lie along a straight line (180°).
They measure 42°, x°, and 65°.
Find the value of x.
questions.worked_solution: Angles on a straight line add to 180°. x = 180 − (42 + 65) = 180 − 107 = 73°.

questions.question:
In a kite ABCD, the two unequal vertex angles
measure 70° and 50°.
What is the size of each of the two equal opposite angles?
questions.worked_solution: Angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360°. Remaining angle sum = 360° − (70° + 50°) = 240°. Each equal angle = 240° ÷ 2 = 120°.

questions.question:
Four angles meet at a single point (a full revolution).
Three of the angles measure 110°, 85°, and 95°.
What is the size of the fourth angle?

A non-convex (arrowhead) quadrilateral has three acute
interior angles measuring 35°, 45°, and 50°.
What is the size of the fourth (reflex) interior angle?
questions.worked_solution: The interior angles of any quadrilateral sum to 360°. Reflex angle = 360° − (35° + 45° + 50°) = 360° − 130° = 230°.

questions.question:
Two interior angles of a triangle measure 48° and 67°.
What is the size of the third interior angle?
questions.worked_solution: Angle sum of a triangle is 180°. Third angle = 180° − (48° + 67°) = 65°.

questions.question:
An exterior angle of a triangle measures 135°.
One of the opposite interior angles is 60°.
What is the size of the other opposite interior angle?
questions.worked_solution: By the exterior angle theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 135° − 60° = 75°.

questions.question:
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
One of the acute angles formed measures 62°.
What is the size of each obtuse angle formed?
questions.worked_solution: Adjacent angles along the parallel line are supplementary: 180° − 62° = 118°.

questions.question:
Triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = AC.
The apex angle ∠BAC measures 44°.
What is the size of the base angle ∠ABC?
questions.worked_solution: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. ∠ABC = (180° − 44°) ÷ 2 = 136° ÷ 2 = 68°.

questions.question:
Using the formula S = 180 × (n − 2),
calculate the interior angle sum of a hexagon (6 sides).

Two co-interior angles between parallel lines
measure (2x + 10)° and (x + 20)°.
Solve for x.

Calculate the size of ONE interior angle
of a regular octagon (8 equal sides and angles).

Two parallel horizontal lines are joined by a V-shaped
bend pointing to the right. The top acute angle with the
parallel line is 38° and the bottom acute angle is 54°.
What is the size of the angle at the tip of the bend?
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw two parallel horizontal lines with arrows. Connect them with a V-shaped bend pointing right. Label the top acute interior angle 38°, the bottom acute interior angle 54°, and the vertex angle at the tip x°.]
questions.worked_solution: Draw a third parallel line through the vertex of the bend. By alternate angles on parallel lines, x = 38° + 54° = 92°.

questions.question:
Two triangles both have side lengths of 6 cm and 9 cm,
with the included angle between those sides equal to 50°.
Which congruence test proves they are congruent
('SSS', 'SAS', 'AAS', or 'RHS')?
questions.worked_solution: Two pairs of matching sides and the included angle between them satisfy the Side-Angle-Side (SAS) congruence test.

questions.question:
The four interior angles of a quadrilateral are
x°, (x + 20)°, (2x − 10)°, and (2x + 50)°.
Find the value of x.

In the diagram, ΔABC is similar to ΔAED (DE || BC).
If AE = 6 cm, AB = 15 cm, and AD = 8 cm,
how long is the full side AC (in cm)?
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a large triangle ABC with internal line DE parallel to base BC. Label AE = 6 cm, full right side AB = 15 cm, and top left side AD = 8 cm.]

questions.question:
The diagonals of a rhombus measure 16 cm and 30 cm.
Since the diagonals bisect each other at 90°, they form
four right-angled triangles with legs 8 cm and 15 cm.
Find the PERIMETER of the rhombus.
questions.worked_solution: Side length s = √(8² + 15²) = √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 cm. Perimeter of rhombus = 4 × 17 = 68 cm.

questions.question:
In this right-angled triangle, side AB = 5, base BC = 12,
and hypotenuse AC = 13.
Calculate the area of triangle ABC.
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a right-angled triangle ABC with the right angle at B. Label side AB = 5, side BC = 12, and hypotenuse AC = 13. Mark angle C with an arc.]
questions.worked_solution: A = ½ × base × perpendicular height = ½ × 12 × 5 = 30 square units.

questions.question: Convert 3.4 kilometres (km) into metres (m).

The square shown has a side length of 5 m.
A second square has a perimeter 3 times as large.
What is the AREA of the second square (in m²)?
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a square with identical tick marks on all four sides. Label the bottom side '5 m'.]
questions.worked_solution: First square side = 5 m, so second square side = 3 × 5 = 15 m. Area = 15 × 15 = 225 m².

questions.question:
A parallelogram has a base of 11 cm, a slanted side
of 9 cm, and a perpendicular height of 7 cm.
Calculate its area (in cm²).
questions.worked_solution: Area of parallelogram = base × perpendicular height = 11 × 7 = 77 cm².

questions.question:
A kite has diagonals of length 14 cm and 9 cm.
Calculate the area of the kite (in cm²).

A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 cm
and a length of 15 cm.
What is the width of the rectangle (in cm)?

A rectangular swimming pool is 8 m long, 4 m wide,
and 2 m deep. Given that 1 m³ = 1 kilolitre (1000 L),
how many kilolitres (kL) of water does the full pool hold?
questions.worked_solution: Volume = 8 × 4 × 2 = 64 m³. Since 1 m³ = 1 kL, capacity = 64 kL.

questions.question:
A trapezium has parallel sides of 8 cm and 14 cm,
and a perpendicular height of 6 cm.
Calculate the area of the trapezium (in cm²).

A rectangular shipping crate is 10 m long, 5 m wide, and 2 m high.
What is the total surface area of the prism (in m²)?

Calculate the circumference of a circle with a diameter
of 14 cm, rounded to the nearest whole number (in cm).
(Use C = π × d)
questions.worked_solution: C = π × 14 ≈ 43.98 cm, which rounds to 44 cm.

questions.question:
Two similar rectangles have a scale factor of 4.
The small rectangle has a width of 3 cm and length of 5 cm.
What is the AREA of the large rectangle (in cm²)?
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw two rectangles side-by-side. The smaller rectangle has a width labelled '3 cm'. A curved arrow points to the larger rectangle with the text 'Scale Factor 4'. The width of the larger rectangle is labelled 'w'.]
questions.worked_solution: Large width = 3 × 4 = 12 cm. Large length = 5 × 4 = 20 cm. Large Area = 12 × 20 = 240 cm².

questions.question:
A train departs Central Station at 14:35
and arrives at its destination at 17:20.
How many minutes did the journey take?
questions.worked_solution: 14:35 to 17:35 is 3 hours (180 minutes). Subtract 15 minutes to reach 17:20: 180 − 15 = 165 minutes.

questions.question:
The rectangular garden shown measures 12 m by 8 m.
A uniform concrete path 1 m wide is built all the way around
the OUTSIDE of the garden.
What is the area of the path alone (in m²)?
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a simple rectangle labelled '12 m' along the top length and '8 m' along the right width.]
questions.worked_solution: Outer rectangle = (12 + 2) × (8 + 2) = 14 × 10 = 140 m². Inner garden = 12 × 8 = 96 m². Path area = 140 − 96 = 44 m².

questions.question:
Calculate the area of a circle with a radius of 5 cm.
Round your answer to the nearest whole number (in cm²).
(Use the formula A = π × r²)
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a circle with a dot in the centre. Draw a solid line from the centre to the edge, labelled 'r = 5 cm'.]
questions.worked_solution: Area = π × 5² = 78.5398... Rounds up to 79 cm².

questions.question:
A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm.
Calculate its volume (in cm³), rounded to the nearest
whole number. (Use V = π × r² × h and the π button)
questions.worked_solution: V = π × 4² × 10 = 160π ≈ 502.65 cm³, which rounds to 503 cm³.

questions.question:
A trapezium has an area of 54 cm² and a perpendicular
height of 6 cm. One of its parallel sides is 7 cm long.
Find the length of the other parallel side (in cm).

Convert an area of 3.5 m² into square centimetres (cm²).
(Remember: 1 m = 100 cm)

A triangular prism has a front triangular face with an
area of 12 m², and a total length (depth) of 10 m.
What is the volume of the prism (in m³)?
(Use the formula V = A × h)
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a 3D triangular prism. Shade the front triangular face and label it 'Area = 12 m²'. Label the long receding edge of the prism '10 m'.]
questions.worked_solution: Volume = Area of cross-section × perpendicular height (length) = 12 × 10 = 120 m³.

questions.question:
A rectangular garden measures 10 m by 6 m. A concreter
removes a semicircular patio (diameter = 6 m)
and a triangular flower bed (base = 4 m, height = 3 m).
What area is left over for grass, correct to 1 decimal place?
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a 10 m by 6 m rectangle. On one of the 6 m ends, draw an inward-curving semicircle of diameter 6 m. Inside the rectangle, draw a triangle with base 4 m and perpendicular height 3 m. Shade the remaining grass area.]
questions.worked_solution: Rectangle = 10 × 6 = 60 m². Semicircle (r = 3) = ½ × π × 3² = 14.14 m². Triangle = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 m². Grass = 60 − 14.14 − 6 = 39.9 m².

questions.question:
Solve for x:
4x − 9 = 27
Evaluate 3x − 2y when x = 4 and y = −5.

Solve for m:
(m ÷ 4) + 7 = 15

Simplify by collecting like terms:
7a + 4b − 2a + 5b

To check if x = 6 is the correct solution to
5(x − 2) = 3x + 4, you substitute x = 6 into both sides.
What is the numerical value of the Right-Hand Side (RHS)?
questions.worked_solution: RHS = 3(6) + 4 = 18 + 4 = 22. (Since LHS = 5(6 − 2) = 20 ≠ RHS, x = 6 is not the solution).

questions.question:
Expand the brackets:
4(3x − 5)

Solve for x:
3(2x − 5) = 27

Factorise completely using the highest common factor:
12x + 18
questions.worked_solution: The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6. Factorising gives 6(2x + 3).

questions.question:
Solve for x:
7x − 4 = 3x + 28

On the Cartesian plane, in which quadrant
(1, 2, 3, or 4) does the point (−4, 7) lie?
questions.worked_solution: Negative x-coordinate and positive y-coordinate places the point in Quadrant 2 (top-left).

questions.question:
The straight line on the grid passes through (0, 2) and (3, 8),
following the linear rule y = 2x + 2.
Use this equation to find the value of x when y = 30.
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a Cartesian plane showing a straight line passing through a point on the y-axis labelled '(0, 2)' and a point further up and to the right labelled '(3, 8)'. Add a dashed right-angled triangle showing the rise and run between the points.]

questions.question:
Find the x-coordinate of the midpoint
of the interval joining (−2, 5) and (10, 9).

Let x be an unknown number.
When x is tripled and then decreased by 11,
the result is equal to x increased by 25.
Find the value of x.

A straight line passes through (1, 3) and (5, 15).
Calculate the gradient (m = rise ÷ run) of this line.

Solve for x:
(3x + 5) ÷ 4 = 8

Expand and simplify to solve for x:
4(x + 3) − 2(x − 1) = 26

A rectangle has length (2x + 3) cm and width x cm.
If its total perimeter is 42 cm,
find the value of x.

The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 81.
Let the smallest number be x, so the next two are
(x + 2) and (x + 4).
What is the LARGEST of the three numbers?

On the Cartesian plane, B is at (−1, 5) and C is at (5, −3).
Find the exact straight-line
distance between Point B and Point C.
questions.svg_prompt: [SVG Prompt: Draw a Cartesian plane with axes from −6 to 6. Plot Point B at (−1, 5) and Point C at (5, −3), connected by a straight line segment.]

questions.question:
Evaluate:
−7 + 12 − 9

Evaluate:
8 − (−13)
questions.worked_solution: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.question:
Using the order of operations (BIDMAS), evaluate:
5 + 3 × 8 − 6 ÷ 2

At midnight in Thredbo the temperature was −4°C.
By midday it rose by 13°C, then dropped 11°C by evening.
What was the evening temperature (in °C)?

Evaluate using the order of operations:
4 × (9 − 5)² − 12

Evaluate:
(−3)² + (−2)³

A submarine is at an elevation of −140 m.
It dives 35 m per minute for 4 minutes,
then rises 95 m. What is its new elevation
(in m, include the − sign)?

In a maths quiz, a correct answer scores +4 points
and a wrong answer scores −2 points.
If Sam gets 14 correct and 5 wrong, what is Sam's total score?

Two integers have a product of −36 and a sum of −5.
What is the SMALLER (more negative) of the two integers?
questions.worked_solution: The two integers are −9 and 4 (−9 × 4 = −36 and −9 + 4 = −5). The smaller integer is −9.

questions.question: Write the fraction 18/24 in its simplest form.
questions.worked_solution: Divide numerator and denominator by their HCF of 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 24 ÷ 6 = 4 → 3/4.

questions.question: Calculate 3/5 of 85.
Calculate 15% of $240.
Convert the fraction 7/20 into a percentage.

Calculate 2/3 + 1/4.
Write your answer as a simplified fraction.

A $160 pair of sneakers is discounted by 25%.
What is the sale price?

A skateboard costs $85 before GST.
If 10% GST is added, what is the final price?

A bicycle is bought for $200 and sold for $250.
Calculate the percentage profit.

Evaluate (3/4) ÷ (9/8).
Write your answer as a simplified fraction.

After a 20% discount, a hoodie costs $96.
What was the ORIGINAL price before the discount?

A $200 share rises in value by 10% on Monday,
then falls by 10% on Tuesday.
What is the share worth at the end of Tuesday?
Write the ratio 24 : 36 in its simplest form.
questions.worked_solution: Divide both sides by their HCF of 12: 24 ÷ 12 = 2, 36 ÷ 12 = 3 → 2 : 3.

questions.question:
Find the missing value x in this equivalent ratio:
3 : 5 = 18 : x
questions.worked_solution: 3 × 6 = 18, so multiply the second term by 6: x = 5 × 6 = 30.

questions.question:
A car uses 36 litres of petrol to travel 450 km.
Calculate the car's fuel rate in km per litre.

Simplify the ratio 40 cm : 2 m
by converting to the same units first.
questions.worked_solution: 2 m = 200 cm. Ratio = 40 : 200. Divide both by 40 → 1 : 5.

questions.question:
Divide $120 in the ratio 3 : 5.
What is the value of the LARGER share?

A train travels 270 km in 3 hours at a constant speed.
At this same speed, how far does it travel in 5 hours (in km)?
questions.worked_solution: Speed = 270 ÷ 3 = 90 km/h. Distance in 5 hours = 90 × 5 = 450 km.

questions.question:
Pack A has 6 muffins for $9.00.
Pack B has 8 muffins for $10.40.
What is the unit price (in dollars) of the BETTER VALUE pack?
questions.worked_solution: Pack A: $9.00 ÷ 6 = $1.50 each. Pack B: $10.40 ÷ 8 = $1.30 each. Better value is Pack B at $1.30 each.

questions.question:
The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 4 : 7.
If there are 28 girls in the club,
how many students are in the club IN TOTAL?

A prize of $180 is shared in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4.
What is the value of the MIDDLE share?

On a map with a scale of 1 : 50 000,
two towns are 6 cm apart.
What is the actual distance between them (in km)?

A cyclist rides 15 km in 1 hour,
then rides another 60 km in 2 hours.
What is the cyclist's average speed (in km/h)?
questions.worked_solution: Total distance = 15 + 60 = 75 km. Total time = 1 + 2 = 3 hours. Average speed = 75 ÷ 3 = 25 km/h.

questions.question:
Evaluate:
5² + √64

Find the Highest Common Factor (HCF)
of 36 and 48.

Find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
of 12 and 18.

Using the zero index law, evaluate:
7 × 5^0 + 3^0
questions.worked_solution: Any non-zero number to the power of 0 equals 1: 7 × 1 + 1 = 8.

questions.question:
Using index laws, simplify and evaluate:
(2^5 × 2^4) ÷ 2^6

Evaluate:
(cube root of 27) + 4³

A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of
6 cm and 8 cm.
Use Pythagoras' theorem to find the hypotenuse (in cm).

A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm
and one shorter side of 5 cm.
Find the length of the other shorter side (in cm).

A 10 m ladder leans against a vertical wall
with its foot 6 m away from the base of the wall.
How high up the wall does the ladder reach (in m)?

A rectangular paddock is 24 m long and 7 m wide.
A straight fence is built diagonally from one corner
to the opposite corner. How long is the fence (in m)?

A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 cm
and a base of 15 cm.
Calculate the AREA of the triangle (in cm²).

A fair 6-sided die is rolled once.
What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
Give your answer as a simplified fraction.
questions.worked_solution: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6 (2 outcomes out of 6). 2/6 simplifies to 1/3.

questions.question:
The probability that it rains in Sydney tomorrow is 0.35.
What is the probability that it does NOT rain
(as a decimal)?

A bag of lollies holds 5 red, 7 green, and 8 yellow snakes.
What is the probability of picking a red snake?
(Give as a simplified fraction or decimal)

A spinner lands on blue with a probability of 0.3.
If you spin it 200 times, how many times
would you expect it to land on blue?

One card is drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck.
What is the probability of drawing a Heart?
(Give as a simplified fraction)
questions.worked_solution: There are 13 Hearts in 52 cards. 13/52 simplifies to 1/4.

questions.question:
A jar contains 6 blue, 9 red, and 5 white marbles.
What is the probability of NOT picking a blue marble?
(Give as a simplified fraction or decimal)

One letter is chosen at random from the word
MATHEMATICS.
What is the probability that it is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U)?
Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.worked_solution: MATHEMATICS has 11 letters, of which 4 are vowels (A, E, A, I). Probability = 4/11.

questions.question:
In a class of 30 students, 18 play soccer,
15 play basketball, and 7 play BOTH sports.
How many students play NEITHER sport?
questions.worked_solution: Play at least one sport = 18 + 15 − 7 = 26. Neither = 30 − 26 = 4 students.

questions.question:
In a survey of 40 students, 22 like maths,
19 like science, and 6 like neither subject.
How many students like BOTH maths and science?

In a class of 25 students: 10 boys play sport,
4 boys do not, 8 girls play sport, and 3 girls do not.
What is the probability a random student is a girl
who plays sport? (Give as a simplified fraction or decimal)
questions.worked_solution: 8 girls play sport out of 25 students total: 8/25 = 0.32.

questions.question:
A bag contains 12 blue marbles and some red marbles.
If the probability of randomly picking a blue marble
is 3/5, how many RED marbles are in the bag?
questions.worked_solution: 3 parts = 12 blue marbles → 1 part = 4 marbles. Total = 5 × 4 = 20 marbles. Red = 20 − 12 = 8.
